body: At a wildlife reserve, Sana kept watching the river level and the bank for signs that rising water might endanger the camp. Her team described her as “vigilant”. Which phrase is closest in meaning to “vigilant” as used here?
options: ["Checking the area only at irregular intervals","Being careful to notice signs of possible danger or trouble","Paying close attention to every detail","Showing no interest in what is happening"]
explanation: “Vigilant” means being very careful to notice signs of danger or trouble, which matches Sana’s attention to signs that rising water might endanger the camp. Paying attention to every detail is a different quality, while the other options describe irregular checking or lack of interest.

body:
Arrange the following four sentences from a fictional account to form a coherent paragraph.
(A) After the votes were counted, the teacher wrote the chosen title on the story's cover.
(B) The teacher began by asking pupils to suggest titles for their shared story.
(C) After recounting those events, the account makes no claim that voting is always the best way to choose a title.
(D) She gathered the proposed titles and read the full list aloud; only then did the class vote on titles on that list.
Choose the correct sequence from the options given below:
explanation: Sentence B introduces the teacher asking for title suggestions, and sentence D then describes reading the list before the vote. Sentence A follows the vote and its count; sentence C comes last because it refers to the events recounted in the account.

topic: Match the Following: focus on this supplied section: aggressive or unfriendly and ready to argue or fight. Test a distinct implication, application or calculation supported by it.
body:
Match each situation in List-I with the word in List-II that best describes it. Each word in List-II is to be used once.

List-I
(A) A staff member spends several weeks on a task that demands great effort and energy.
(B) When challenged, a colleague responds in an unfriendly way and seems ready to argue.
(C) At a gathering, a person enjoys being among other people.
(D) A training video is uninteresting and seems to go on for too long.

List-II
(I) "hostile"
(II) "gregarious"
(III) "tedious"
(IV) "arduous"

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation: A describes a task involving sustained effort, so it is arduous. B describes someone unfriendly and ready to argue, so it is hostile; C describes enjoying other people’s company, so it is gregarious; and D describes something uninteresting that lasts too long, so it is tedious.

body: At a project meeting, Rohan presented a proposal confirmed to be his genuine, original work. While discussing it, he treated his judgement as superior to everyone else’s and dismissed the effects of his decision on colleagues as unimportant. He remained friendly, did not seek an argument or fight, and was not watching for signs of danger or trouble. Which word best describes his manner toward his colleagues?
options: ["arrogant","vigilant","hostile","authentic"]
explanation: Rohan acts as though his judgement is superior and gives little consideration to how his decision affects colleagues, so “arrogant” best describes his manner. “Vigilant” concerns watching for signs of danger or trouble, while the stem says he was not doing so; it also rules out “hostile” by stating that he remained friendly and did not seek an argument or fight. “Authentic” describes whether something is real and not a copy, which applies to the proposal’s stated originality, not to Rohan’s manner.

body: Though Rohan spoke little during meetings, he actively sought company during breaks, joined group activities and enjoyed spending time with colleagues. His teammates described him as “gregarious”. Which word is the clearest antonym of “gregarious” in this context?
options: ["taciturn","convivial","solitary","amiable"]
explanation: “Gregarious” means “liking to be with other people”. “Solitary” expresses the contrasting idea of being alone. Rohan’s quietness concerns how much he speaks; the context makes clear that he enjoys company.

body: While reviewing an inventory, Sana checked each record and paid close attention to its details. Her supervisor described her work as “meticulous”. Which phrase is closest in meaning to “meticulous”?
options: ["Happening only occasionally or at intervals that are not regular","Paying careful attention to every detail","Not supporting one person or group more than another","Having or showing no interest in somebody or something"]
explanation: Sana’s close attention to the details matches the meaning of “meticulous”. The other choices describe irregular occurrence, impartiality, and lack of interest, respectively.

body:
Arrange the following four sentences in the order in which the events are reported.
(A) Each participant practised the assigned speaking part individually.
(B) Finally, the group performed the scene together using the parts they had practised.
(C) The group first read a short scene together.
(D) After that reading, the group assigned its speaking parts.
Choose the correct sequence from the options given below:
(A) C-D-A-B
(B) D-C-A-B
(C) C-A-D-B
(D) C-D-B-A
explanation: The group read the scene first, then assigned its speaking parts. The members practised those assigned parts before the group performed the scene, so the reported order is C-D-A-B.

topic: Match the Following: focus on this supplied section: logical and well organized; easy to understand and clear. Test a distinct implication, application or calculation supported by it.
body:
Use "coherent" to mean that ideas are logically organised and that the writing is easy to understand and clear. Each entry describes a report about a process; classify it using only these two features.

List-I
(A) The report presents the stages in an order that follows the process, and explains each stage clearly and in wording that is easy to understand.
(B) The report presents the stages in an order that follows the process, but the explanations are unclear and difficult to understand.
(C) The report presents the stages in an order that does not follow the process, but explains each stage clearly and in wording that is easy to understand.
(D) The report presents the stages in an order that does not follow the process, and the explanations are unclear and difficult to understand.

List-II
(I) Both features are present
(II) Only logical organisation is present
(III) Only clarity and ease of understanding are present
(IV) Neither feature is present

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation: A has both logical organisation and clarity, while B has logical organisation but not clarity. C has clarity but not logical organisation, and D has neither feature; therefore the matches are (A)-(I), (B)-(II), (C)-(III) and (D)-(IV).

body: The archive assignment would take several hours and require checking many entries. Rina nevertheless requested it, saying she wanted to do it and needed no encouragement. Which phrase is the clearest antonym of "reluctant" in this context?
options: ["Hesitating to undertake it because she does not want to","Being keen to undertake it and ready to begin","Paying careful attention to every detail while doing it","Finding it long and uninteresting"]
explanation: “Reluctant” means hesitating to do something because one does not want to do it. Rina says she wants the assignment and requests it without needing encouragement, so being keen to undertake it expresses the opposite attitude. Paying attention to detail concerns how a task is done, while finding it long and uninteresting concerns the task’s duration and interest.

body:
Read the sentence and choose the phrase closest in meaning to “ambiguous” as used here.
After reading the line “They saw her duck,” one classmate said it meant that they watched her lower her head; another said it meant that they saw the bird belonging to her. The teacher described the line as ambiguous.
options: ["expressing an opinion firmly and confidently","not favouring one person or group over another","open to more than one interpretation","no longer used because something new has replaced it"]
explanation: The line is ambiguous because the classmates understand it in two different ways: they watched her lower her head, or they saw her bird. Thus, “open to more than one interpretation” is the closest phrase.

topic: Match the Following: focus on this supplied section: only present in small amounts or numbers and often spread over a large area. Test a distinct implication, application or calculation supported by it.
body:
Match each situation in List-I with the word in List-II that best describes it. Each word in List-II is to be used once.

List-I
(A) A region has only a few villages, spread across a wide area.
(B) A person can perform many different kinds of tasks.
(C) A person recovers quickly after an unpleasant shock.
(D) A worker carries out duties with care and effort.

List-II
(I) "Diligent"
(II) "Sparse"
(III) "Resilient"
(IV) "Versatile"

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation: The villages are sparse because they are few and spread over a wide area. The other descriptions match versatile, resilient and diligent, respectively, by the abilities or qualities stated in each case.

body: An official states that a storm will miss the city. A journalist doubts that the statement is true and asks for evidence before accepting it. Which word best describes the journalist’s attitude towards the statement?
options: ["authentic","vigilant","sceptical","optimistic"]
explanation: The journalist doubts that the official’s statement is true, so “sceptical” is the best fit. “Authentic” concerns whether something is genuine rather than a copy, “vigilant” concerns noticing signs of danger or trouble, and “optimistic” expresses an expectation of good things.

body: In a planning meeting, Dev clearly stated the outcome he wanted and explained his recommendation with confidence so that the group would take his view seriously. A colleague described Dev as “assertive”. Which phrase is closest in meaning to “assertive” as used here?
options: ["Expressing opinions or wishes firmly and confidently so that others take notice","Expecting good things to happen or believing that something will succeed","Feeling very happy and excited because of a good event","Involving a great deal of effort and energy over a period of time"]
explanation: Dev expresses what he wants and thinks firmly and confidently so that others take notice, which matches the meaning of “assertive”. The other options describe optimism, elation and arduous effort, respectively.

(A) He first made a copy of the original recording.
(B) The original was retained throughout the stated process.
(C) He then edited the copy to reduce the noise.
(D) In this fictional account, Aman found that the recording of his interview contained background noise.
Choose the correct sequence from the options given below:

body:
Match each situation in List-I with the assessment in List-II. Match the person’s stated preference separately from whether the person is currently alone or with others.

List-I
(A) Asha joins an optional group gathering because she says she enjoys being with other people.
(B) Bilal works alone because his task requires him to work in a quiet room; he says he likes being with other people.
(C) Charu declines an optional group gathering and says she prefers spending time alone.
(D) Deepa attends a team meeting because participation is required; she says she prefers spending her free time alone.

List-II
(I) Likes company and chooses it voluntarily.
(II) Likes company but is alone because the task requires it.
(III) Prefers being alone and chooses it voluntarily.
(IV) Prefers being alone but joins others because participation is required.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation: The definition concerns liking to be with other people, so match each person’s stated preference separately from their current situation. Asha chooses company because she enjoys it; Bilal likes company but works alone because his task requires it. Charu prefers being alone and chooses it, while Deepa prefers being alone but attends because participation is required. Therefore, option C gives the correct one-to-one matching.

body: A report claims that a ferry will arrive by noon. Priya asks questions about the forecast, but she is described as “sceptical” because she doubts that the claim is true. Later, she accepts the claim as true. Which word best expresses an attitude opposite to her initial attitude?
options: ["inquisitive","convinced","sporadic","tedious"]
explanation: “Sceptical” means having doubts about whether a claim is true. Priya’s initial attitude is one of doubt, whereas being convinced that the claim is true expresses the opposite attitude. The other options refer to interest in learning, irregular occurrence, and something prolonged and uninteresting, respectively.

body: A company has received ₹2,40,000 as calls in advance. Subsequently, calls of ₹80,000 and ₹95,000 become due, and the full amount of each call is adjusted against the advance. No other advance is received or adjusted. What is the balance in Calls in Advance Account immediately after these adjustments? Ignore interest.
explanation: The calls in advance are adjusted towards the calls when they become due. The remaining balance is ₹2,40,000 − (₹80,000 + ₹95,000) = ₹65,000.

body:
A firm admits T. Before admission, P, Q, R and S have profit shares of 1/2, 1/4, 1/8 and 1/8, respectively. After admission, their respective profit shares are P 1/3, Q 1/8, R 1/24 and S 1/12; T’s share is 5/12. Match each old partner with that partner’s individual sacrifice in profit share.

List-I
(A) P: old share 1/2; new share 1/3
(B) Q: old share 1/4; new share 1/8
(C) R: old share 1/8; new share 1/24
(D) S: old share 1/8; new share 1/12

List-II
(I) 1/24
(II) 1/12
(III) 1/8
(IV) 1/6

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation: Each partner’s sacrifice is the old share minus the new share. The sacrifices are P: 1/6, Q: 1/8, R: 1/12 and S: 1/24, giving the mapping (A)-(IV), (B)-(III), (C)-(II) and (D)-(I).

body:
A company has forfeited 500 shares. It subsequently reissues 200 of those shares, while the other 300 remain unreissued. Consider the following statements about the reissue:
(A) Capital profit transferred to Capital Reserve can relate only to the shares reissued.
(B) Any discount allowed on reissue is debited to Share Forfeiture Account.
(C) The entire balance of Share Forfeiture Account for all 500 shares may be transferred to Capital Reserve after only 200 shares are reissued.
(D) Forfeited shares may be reissued only at par.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: ["(A) and (B) only","(A) and (C) only","(B) and (D) only","(C) and (D) only"]
explanation: Capital profit arises only in respect of forfeited shares that are reissued, so it can relate only to the 200 reissued shares; the whole balance for all 500 shares cannot be transferred after only 200 are reissued. Any discount allowed on reissue is debited to Share Forfeiture Account. Forfeited shares may also be reissued at a premium or at a discount, so statements (C) and (D) are incorrect.

On admission of a new partner, a firm has an accumulated profit of ₹1,20,000 in its General Reserve that has not been transferred to any partner’s account. The old partners, P and Q, shared profits in the ratio 3:2. Arrange the following steps for distributing this accumulated profit.
(A) Identify ₹1,20,000 as the accumulated profit to be distributed.
(B) Restrict the distribution to P and Q and use their old profit-sharing ratio of 3:2.
(C) Calculate P’s share as ₹72,000 and Q’s share as ₹48,000.
(D) Transfer the respective shares to P’s and Q’s capital/current accounts.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation: The accumulated profit is distributed among the old partners in their old profit-sharing ratio, and the new partner is not entitled to a share in it. P’s share is ₹1,20,000 × 3/5 = ₹72,000, and Q’s share is ₹1,20,000 × 2/5 = ₹48,000. The respective amounts are then transferred to P’s and Q’s capital/current accounts.

body:
Four garment-manufacturing companies report the following figures for one accounting period. “Operating cash” means net cash generated from operating activities. All amounts are in ₹ lakh.
Aarav Garments: operating cash ₹18 lakh; cash required to maintain operating capability ₹5 lakh; dividends ₹3 lakh; new investments ₹6 lakh; loan repayments ₹4 lakh.
Bela Garments: operating cash ₹18 lakh; cash required to maintain operating capability ₹5 lakh; dividends ₹4 lakh; new investments ₹6 lakh; loan repayments ₹4 lakh.
Charu Garments: operating cash ₹20 lakh; cash required to maintain operating capability ₹6 lakh; dividends ₹4 lakh; new investments ₹7 lakh; loan repayments ₹4 lakh.
Dev Garments: operating cash ₹17 lakh; cash required to maintain operating capability ₹4 lakh; dividends ₹3 lakh; new investments ₹6 lakh; loan repayments ₹5 lakh.
Assume each listed requirement must be met during the period, opening cash is nil, and no cash from investing activities, financing activities or any other source is available for these requirements. There are no other relevant cash requirements or sources.
Which company can meet all four listed requirements from operating cash alone?
options: ["Aarav Garments","Bela Garments","Charu Garments","Dev Garments"]
explanation: Aarav’s four requirements total ₹5 lakh + ₹3 lakh + ₹6 lakh + ₹4 lakh = ₹18 lakh, exactly equal to its operating cash. The stated principle treats cash from operations as an indicator of whether operations have generated sufficient cash to meet these kinds of requirements without external financing. The other companies’ requirements total ₹19 lakh, ₹21 lakh and ₹18 lakh respectively, each exceeding their operating cash.

The amount of cash from operations’ indicates the internal solvency level of the company, and is regarded as the key indicator of the extent to which the operations of the enterprise have generated sufficient cash flows to maintain the operating capability of the enterprise, paying dividends, making of new investments and repaying of loans without recourse to external source of financing. Cash Flow Statement 249 As per AS-3, an enterprise should report cash flows from operating activities either by using :  Direct method whereby major classes of gross cash receipts and gross cash payments are disclosed; or  Indirect method whereby net profit or loss is duly adjusted for the effects of (1) transactions of a non-cash nature, (2) any deferrals or accruals of past/future operating cash receipts, and (3) items of income or expenses associated with investing or financing cash flows. It is important to mention here that under indirect method, the starting point is net profit/loss before taxation and extra ordinary items as per Statement of Profit and Loss of the enterprise. Then this amount is for non-cash items, etc., adjusted for ascertaining cash flows from operating activities. Accordingly, cash flow from operating activities can be determined using either the Direct method or the Indirect method.The direct method provides information which is useful in estimating future cash flows. But such information is not available under the indirect method. However, in practice, indirect method is mostly used by the companies for arriving at the net cash flow from operating activities. body: A partnership has a profit remaining after all appropriations, which is to be distributed among its partners. It maintains a separate current account for each partner. Only the distribution of this remaining profit is being recorded. Which journal entry records the distribution?
options: ["Partners’ Current A/cs (individually) Dr.; To Profit and Loss Appropriation A/c","Profit and Loss Appropriation A/c Dr.; To Partners’ Current A/cs (individually)","Profit and Loss A/c Dr.; To Partners’ Current A/cs (individually)","Profit and Loss Appropriation A/c Dr.; To Partners’ Capital A/cs (individually)"]
explanation: The remaining profit is recorded by debiting Profit and Loss Appropriation A/c and crediting the partners’ accounts individually. Since the firm maintains separate current accounts for its partners, those accounts are credited. Option A reverses the entry, option C debits Profit and Loss A/c, and option D credits capital accounts rather than the current accounts specified in the stem.

body: A company buys back 12,000 fully paid shares with a nominal value of ₹10 per share at ₹15 per share. The buy-back is made entirely out of free reserves. How much must be transferred to the Capital Redemption Reserve Account?
explanation: When shares are bought back out of free reserves, the transfer to the Capital Redemption Reserve Account equals the nominal value of the shares bought back. The total nominal value is 12,000 × ₹10 = ₹1,20,000; the repurchase price does not determine this transfer.

body:
In each independent case, a new partner brings a cash premium for goodwill, and the existing partners sacrifice part of their shares. Match each situation in List-I with its accounting treatment in List-II.

List-I
(A) The new partner pays the premium directly and privately to the existing partners.
(B) The premium is received through the firm and initially credited to Premium for Goodwill A/c.
(C) The premium is received through the firm and initially credited to the new partner’s capital account before distribution to the sacrificing partners.
(D) The premium has been credited to the existing partners’ capital accounts in their sacrificing ratio, and they retain the amount in the business.

List-II
(I) No entry is passed in the firm’s books.
(II) Bank A/c Dr. to Premium for Goodwill A/c; then Goodwill A/c Dr. to the sacrificing partners’ capital accounts individually.
(III) Bank A/c Dr. to the new partner’s capital account; then the new partner’s capital account Dr. to the sacrificing partners’ capital accounts individually.
(IV) No additional entry is passed for retaining the credited amounts in the business.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation: A premium paid directly and privately to the existing partners requires no entry in the firm’s books. When the premium is received through the firm, the entries depend on whether it is credited initially to Premium for Goodwill A/c or to the new partner’s capital account. If the credited amounts are retained in the business, no additional entry is passed.

body:
A company’s Statement of Profit and Loss includes a depreciation expense. For calculating cash flows from operating activities by the indirect method, consider the following statements:
(A) Depreciation is a non-cash item.
(B) Depreciation is treated as a cash outflow from operating activities.
(C) Depreciation is added back to net profit when calculating cash flows from operating activities.
(D) Depreciation is added back because it is a cash outflow from financing activities.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
(A) (A) and (B) only
(B) (A) and (C) only
(C) (B) and (D) only
(D) (C) and (D) only
options: ["(A) and (B) only","(A) and (C) only","(B) and (D) only","(C) and (D) only"]
explanation: Statements (A) and (C) are correct: depreciation is a non-cash item, and the amount charged is added back to net profit when calculating cash flows from operating activities. Depreciation does not itself result in a cash flow. The excerpt identifies finance costs, not depreciation, as a cash outflow on account of financing activity.

Moreover, it also includes certain non-operating items such as interest paid, profit/loss on sale of fixed assets, etc.) and non-cash items (such as depreciation, goodwill written-off, divident declared, etc. Therefore, it becomes necessary to adjust the amount of net profit/loss as shown by Statement of Profit and Loss for arriving at cash flows from operating activities. Let us look at the example : Statement of Profit and Loss Account for the year ended March 31, 2017 Particulars Note Figures in (Rs.) i) Revenue from Operations 1,00,000 ii) Other Income 1 2,000 iii) Total Revenues (i+ii) 1,02,000 iv) Expenses Cost of Materials Consumed 30,000 Purchases of stock-in-trade 10,000 Employees Benefits Expenses 10,000 Finance Costs 5,000 Depreciation 5,000 Other Expenses 12,000 72,000 v) Profit before Tax (iii-iv) 30,000 Note: Other income includes profit on sale of land. The above Statement of Profit and Loss shows the amount of net profit of Rs. 30,000. This has to be adjusted for arriving cash flows from operating activities. Let us take various items one by one. 1. Depreciation is a non-cash item and hence, Rs. 5,000 charged as depreciation does not result in any cash flow. Therefore, this amount must be added back to the net profit. 2. Finance costs of Rs. 5,000 is a cash outflow on account of financing activity. body:
A deceased partner’s claim is being prepared. Assume all applicable credit items and deductions have already been identified and their amounts are known. No other adjustments or payments affect the claim. Arrange the following stages in the order needed to determine and deal with the amount due.

(A) Add the applicable credit items to obtain the gross claim.
(B) Subtract the applicable deductions from the gross claim to obtain the net amount due.
(C) Transfer the resulting claim to the deceased partner’s executors.
(D) Settle the executors’ claim in the same manner as a retired partner’s claim.

Choose the correct sequence:
explanation: The claim includes applicable credit items, and applicable deductions are then made from it to arrive at the net amount due. In the case of death, that claim is transferred to the deceased partner’s executors and settled in the same manner as a retired partner’s claim.

body: Two companies in the same industry differ greatly in size. Each has statements for Year 1 and Year 2, prepared using the same accounting principles. An analyst has set aside the question of trends and must compare the companies’ operating and financing characteristics for Year 2 without letting their different scale dominate the comparison. Which presentation most directly serves this purpose?

explanation: Common-size statements express each item as a percentage of a common item, allowing comparison of operating and financing characteristics across differently sized companies in the same industry. Comparative statements present information for different periods and indicate trends, which does not address the stated same-year comparison between the companies.

Comparative Statements: These are the statements showing the profitability and financial position of a firm for different periods of time in a comparative form to give an idea about the position of two or more periods. It usually applies to the two important financial statements, namely, balance sheet and statement of profit and loss prepared in a comparative form. If this is not the case, the deviation in the use of accounting principles should be mentioned as a footnote. options: ["P alone bears the deficiency.","P and Q bear it in their profit-sharing ratio.","Q alone bears the deficiency.","P and Q bear it equally."]

body: A company’s general assets have a total value of ₹14,00,000. Of these assets, assets worth ₹4,00,000 have been assigned to secured creditors. Assume these are the company’s only assets and assignments. What is the value of the assets covered by a floating charge?
explanation: A floating charge involves all assets except those assigned to secured creditors. The value covered is therefore ₹14,00,000 − ₹4,00,000 = ₹10,00,000.

body:
A company receives calls in advance from shareholders. Match each situation in List-I with the accounting treatment in List-II. Assume no other transaction affects these balances.

List-I
(A) A shareholder pays an amount before the related call is due.
(B) The related call becomes due, and the available advance is adjusted against it.
(C) At the balance-sheet date, the related call is not yet due and the advance remains unadjusted.
(D) Interest on the advance is paid through the bank; assume the Articles provide for this interest.

List-II
(I) Calls in Advance A/c Dr.; To Particular Call A/c.
(II) Show the balance separately under current liabilities—other current liabilities; exclude it from paid-up capital.
(III) Bank A/c Dr.; To Calls in Advance A/c.
(IV) Interest on Calls in Advance A/c Dr.; To Bank A/c.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation: On receipt of calls in advance, Bank A/c is debited and Calls in Advance A/c is credited; when the call becomes due, the advance is debited and the particular call is credited. An unadjusted balance is shown separately under current liabilities and is not added to paid-up capital. When interest is paid through the bank, Interest on Calls in Advance A/c is debited and Bank A/c is credited.

body:
A company incurs a non-recurring cash outflow associated with a flood loss. The activity from which the outflow arises is not specified.
Which statements correctly describe the outflow and its treatment?
(A) The cash flow should be classified and disclosed separately as arising from the relevant operating, investing or financing activity.
(B) Separate disclosure helps users understand the nature of the item and its effect on present and future cash flows.
(C) The outflow must be classified as an investing activity because it is associated with a flood loss.
(D) A flood loss is an example of an extraordinary item.
options: ["(A), (B) and (C) only","(A), (B) and (D) only","(A), (C) and (D) only","(B), (C) and (D) only"]
explanation: A flood loss is an example of an extraordinary item, and the cash flow associated with an extraordinary item is classified and disclosed separately as arising from an operating, investing or financing activity. This separate disclosure helps users understand the item's nature and its effect on present and future cash flows. The stem does not establish that the outflow arises from investing activity, so a flood loss alone does not support that classification.

Extraordinary items are non-recurring in nature and hence cash flows associated with extraordinary items should be classified and disclosed separately as arising from operating, investing or financing activities. This is done to enable users to understand their nature and effect on the present and future cash flows of an enterprise. Interest and Dividend In case of a financial enterprise (whose main business is lending and borrowing), interest paid, interest received and dividend received are classified as operating activities while dividend paid is a financing activity. In case of a non-financial enterprise, as per AS-3, it is considered more appropriate that payment of interest and dividends are classified as financing activities whereas receipt of interest and dividends are classified as investing activities. body:
Partners P, Q and R agree to change their profit-sharing ratio without admitting or retiring any partner. The new ratio gives some partners a larger share of future profits and others a smaller share. Assume any goodwill gain or loss arising from the change is to be adjusted. Arrange the following steps in the logical order:
(A) Record the goodwill adjustment by crediting sacrificing partner(s) and debiting gaining partner(s) with appropriate amounts.
(B) Agree on the new profit-sharing ratio.
(C) Identify the partners who gain or sacrifice future profit shares under the new ratio.
(D) Identify any goodwill gain or loss arising from the change.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation: The partners first agree on the new ratio, then identify who gains and who sacrifices future profit shares. Any goodwill gain or loss arising from the change is then identified and adjusted by crediting the sacrificing partners and debiting the gaining partners.

body: P, Q and R are existing partners, and S is admitted. Their complete old profit shares are P: 1/2, Q: 1/3 and R: 1/6. Their new profit shares, including S’s, are P: 2/5, Q: 1/4, R: 1/5 and S: 3/20. S brings ₹1,32,000 as premium for goodwill through the firm’s bank account. The firm distributes the entire premium among the existing partners in their sacrificing ratio. What amounts are credited to P’s, Q’s and R’s capital accounts, respectively?
explanation: P’s sacrifice is 1/2 − 2/5 = 1/10, and Q’s is 1/3 − 1/4 = 1/12; their sacrificing ratio is therefore 6:5. R’s new share exceeds the old share, so R does not sacrifice a share. Dividing ₹1,32,000 in the ratio 6:5 gives P ₹72,000 and Q ₹60,000.

body: A and B contributed ₹4,00,000 and ₹2,00,000, respectively, to their partnership and share profits equally. Their partnership deed contains no provision for interest on capital. Neither partner added to or withdrew capital during the year. What should be recorded as interest on capital for the year?
options: ["Allow interest to A only, because A contributed more capital.","Allow no interest to either partner.","Allow equal interest to both partners, because they share profits equally.","Allow interest to both partners in the ratio 2:1, matching their capital contributions."]
explanation: Interest on partners’ capital is allowed only when it is expressly agreed among the partners. Since the deed contains no provision for it, neither partner is entitled to interest, regardless of their capital contributions or profit-sharing ratio.

body:
A deceased partner’s claim is being calculated at the date of death. The following amounts are separate, apply to the deceased partner, and have not been adjusted against one another:
Credit balance of capital account: ₹1,20,000
Share of profit up to the date of death: ₹12,000
Interest on capital up to the date of death: ₹4,000
Salary due up to the date of death: ₹6,000
Share of accumulated losses: ₹5,000
Drawings up to the date of death: ₹7,000
Interest on drawings up to the date of death: ₹1,000
Share of loss on revaluation: ₹3,000
No other amount is due or deductible. What is the amount of the deceased partner’s claim before settlement with the executor?
explanation: The capital balance, share of profit, interest on capital and salary due total ₹1,42,000. The accumulated losses, drawings, interest on drawings and share of revaluation loss total ₹16,000 and are deducted. Therefore, the claim is ₹1,42,000 − ₹16,000 = ₹1,26,000.

body:
Match List-I with List-II.

List-I
(A) A firm presents its balance sheet and statement of profit and loss in comparative form for two periods; the figures indicate trends and direction.
(B) An analyst compares the operating and financing characteristics of two differently sized companies in the same industry using common-base percentages.
(C) The accounting principles used in statements being compared differ, and the departure is disclosed in a footnote.
(D) The analysis that expresses each financial statement item as a percentage of a common item is given a particular name.

List-II
(I) Common size statements facilitate comparison of operating and financing characteristics of differently sized companies in the same industry.
(II) Comparative statements show financial position or profitability for different periods, and their figures indicate trends and direction.
(III) Comparative figures require the same accounting principles; departures are mentioned in a footnote.
(IV) Common size analysis is also known as vertical analysis.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation: Comparative statements show a firm's financial position or profitability across periods, and their figures indicate trends and direction; departures from the same accounting principles are mentioned in a footnote. Thus, (A) matches (II) and (C) matches (III). Common size statements support comparison of differently sized companies in the same industry, and common size analysis is also known as vertical analysis, so (B) matches (I) and (D) matches (IV).

Through the analysis of financial statements of various firms, an economist can judge the extent of concentration of economic power and pitfalls in the financial policies pursued. The analysis also provides the basis for many governmental actions relating to licensing, controls, fixing of prices, ceiling on profits, dividend freeze, tax subsidy and other concessions to the corporate sector. 4.4 Tools of Analysis of Financial Statements The most commonly used techniques of financial analysis are as follows: 1. Comparative Statements: These are the statements showing the profitability and financial position of a firm for different periods of time in a comparative form to give an idea about the position of two or more periods. It usually applies to the two important financial statements, namely, balance sheet and statement of profit and loss prepared in a comparative form. The financial data will be comparative only when same accounting principles are used in preparing these statements. If this is not the case, the deviation in the use of accounting principles should be mentioned as a footnote. Comparative figures indicate the trend and direction of financial position and operating results. This analysis is also known as ‘horizontal analysis’. 2. Common Size Statements: These are the statements which indicate the relationship of different items of a financial statement with a common item by expressing each item as a percentage of that common item. The percentage thus calculated can be easily compared with the results of corresponding percentages of the previous year or of some other firms, as the numbers are brought to common base. Such statements also allow an analyst to compare the operating and financing characteristics of two companies of different sizes in the same industry. Thus, common size statements are useful, both, in intra-firm comparisons over different years and also in making inter-firm comparisons for the same year or for several years. body:
A company issues debentures with a nominal value of ₹1,000 each, receives ₹900 per debenture at issue, and undertakes to repay ₹1,100 per debenture on maturity. For this question, an issue proceeds amount below nominal value is an issue at a discount, and a repayment amount above nominal value is redemption at a premium.

(A) The debentures are issued at a discount and redeemable at a premium.
(B) Issue at a discount and redemption at a premium is one of the six situations commonly found in practice.
(C) Because the debentures are issued at a discount, they must be redeemed at par.
(D) Because the debentures are redeemable at a premium, they must have been issued at a premium.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
options: ["(A) and (C) only","(B) and (D) only","(A) and (B) only","(C) and (D) only"]
explanation: The issue proceeds of ₹900 are below the nominal value of ₹1,000, while the repayment of ₹1,100 is above nominal value, so statement (A) is correct. The listed situations include issue at a discount and redemption at a premium, so statement (B) is also correct. That listed combination contradicts statements (C) and (D).

(b) Unsecured Debentures: Unsecured debentures do not have a specific charge on the assets of the company. However, a floating charge may be created on these debentures by default. Normally, these kinds of debentures are not issued. 2.3.2 From the Point of view of Tenure (a) Redeemable Debentures: Redeemable debentures are those which are payable on the expiry of the specific period either in lump sum or in Instalments during the life time of the company. Debentures can be redeemed either at par or at premium. (b) Irredeemable Debentures: Irredeemable debentures are also known as Perpetual Debentures because the company does not give any undertaking for the repayment of money borrowed by issuing such debentures. body:
Arrange the following statements in logical order, beginning with why a company obtains capital from several persons and ending with how their contributions are represented in its accounts.
(A) The contributions are combined in a common account called Share Capital Account.
(B) Since it cannot generate its own capital, the company obtains capital from several persons.
(C) The contributors are shareholders, and their contributions are share capital.
(D) Because shareholders are numerous, a separate capital account is not opened for each.
Choose the correct sequence.
explanation: The logical order is B-C-D-A. The company obtains capital from several persons; they are identified as shareholders and their contributions as share capital; the large number of shareholders explains why a separate account is not opened for each, so the contributions are combined in a Share Capital Account.

The authorised capital can be increased or decreased as per the procedure laid down in the Companies Act. It should be noted that the company need not issue the entire authorised capital for public subscription at a time. Depending upon its requirement, it may issue share capital but in any case, it should not be more than the amount of authorised capital. • Issued Capital: It is that part of the authorised capital which is actually issued to the public for subscription including the shares allotted to vendors and the signatories to the company’s memorandum. In such a condition, three alternatives are available to the directors to deal with the situation: (1) they can accept some applications in full and totally reject the others; (2) they can make a pro-rata allotment to all; and (3) they can adopt a combination of the above two alternatives which happens to be the most common course adopted in practice. body: At the admission of T, X and Y are the existing partners, sharing profits in the ratio 3:2. The agreed profit-sharing ratio after T’s admission is X:Y:T = 4:3:3. The firm has an untransferred reserve of ₹24,000, a general reserve of ₹18,000 and a credit balance of ₹33,000 in the Profit and Loss Account. All three balances are accumulated profits from before T’s admission. What amounts should be allocated to X, Y and T, respectively, from these accumulated profits?
explanation: The accumulated profits total ₹24,000 + ₹18,000 + ₹33,000 = ₹75,000. They are distributed among the existing partners in their old profit-sharing ratio of 3:2, so X receives ₹45,000 and Y receives ₹30,000. T receives no share of these accumulated profits.

body: A new partner brings the agreed goodwill premium in cash through the firm. The firm credits the premium to the existing partners’ capital accounts in their sacrificing ratio. The partners decide to retain the credited amount in the business. Which treatment is required for this decision?
options: ["No additional journal entry is passed.","An additional entry credits the premium to the new partner’s capital account.","An additional entry credits the premium again to the existing partners’ capital accounts in their sacrificing ratio.","An additional entry records withdrawal of the credited amounts by the existing partners."]
explanation: The premium has already been credited to the existing partners’ capital accounts in their sacrificing ratio, and they decide to retain it in the business. In this situation, no additional entry is passed; an additional entry is passed if they decide to withdraw their amounts, in full or in part.

body: Mira, an investor, buys shares from another investor who already owns them. The issuing company is not a party to the sale. Which classification applies to this transaction?
options: ["It is not a secondary-market transaction because Mira is buying rather than selling the shares.","It is not a secondary-market transaction because the seller is another investor rather than the issuer.","It is a secondary-market transaction because Mira buys from another investor.","It cannot be classified as a secondary-market transaction because Mira is not stated to be an investor."]
explanation: A secondary market is defined by an investor buying or selling securities from another investor rather than the issuer. Mira buys the shares from another investor, so this is a secondary-market transaction.

topic: Financial Markets: focus on this supplied section: One of the main objectives of the primary market is to allow companies to raise capital through the issuance of securities. Test a distinct implication, application or calculation supported by it.
body: Northstar Ltd needs funds. Under Plan 1, it issues new securities to investors and receives their payments. Under Plan 2, an existing investor transfers already-issued securities to another investor, and the payment goes to the selling investor, not Northstar Ltd. Which assessment best applies the objective of the primary market?
options: ["Only Plan 2 aligns, because the payment for securities goes to the selling investor.","Both plans align, because each involves securities and an investor payment.","Neither plan aligns, because an issue of securities does not provide capital to the company.","Only Plan 1 aligns, because the company raises capital by issuing securities."]
explanation: Plan 1 lets Northstar Ltd raise capital through the issuance of securities, which is an objective of the primary market. In Plan 2, the payment goes to the selling investor, not to Northstar Ltd.

body:
Consider the following statements about one main objective of the primary market:
I. It is to enable companies to raise capital through issuing securities.
II. It is to enable investors to raise capital through issuing securities.
III. It is to enable companies to raise capital through purchasing securities.
IV. It is to enable companies to invest capital through issuing securities.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: ["I only","II only","III only","IV only"]
explanation: Statement I expresses the objective: enabling companies to raise capital through the issuance of securities. Statement II changes the party raising capital, statement III changes issuance to purchasing securities, and statement IV changes raising capital to investing capital.

body:
Match List-I with List-II. All named persons other than “the issuer” are investors, and each entry describes a single transaction in shares or securities with the stated counterparty.

List-I
(A) Investor P buys shares from Investor Q.
(B) Investor R sells shares to Investor S.
(C) Investor T buys shares from the issuer.
(D) Investor V sells shares to the issuer.

List-II
(I) Secondary-market purchase
(II) Secondary-market sale
(III) Investor purchase from the issuer
(IV) Investor sale to the issuer

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation: A and B are investor-to-investor transactions, so they are respectively a secondary-market purchase and a secondary-market sale. C and D are transactions with the issuer: in C the investor purchases from the issuer, while in D the investor sells to the issuer.

body:
A firm increases its use of debt in its capital structure, with no change in its equity funding. Arrange the following from the financing change to a possible severe consequence. The sequence does not imply that default actually occurs.
(A) A default in meeting the debt commitments may force the business into liquidation.
(B) The increased use of debt raises the firm’s fixed financial charges.
(C) The firm increases its use of debt.
(D) The rise in financial risk represents a greater chance of failing to meet payment obligations.
Choose the correct sequence from the options given below:
explanation: The increase in debt use is followed by an increase in fixed financial charges and financial risk. Financial risk is the chance of failing to meet payment obligations, and a default on the debt commitments may force the business into liquidation. Thus, the order is (C)-(B)-(D)-(A).

Debt and equity differ significantly in their cost and riskiness for the firm. The cost of debt is lower than the cost of equity for a firm because the lender’s risk is lower than the equity shareholder’s risk, since the lender earns an assured return and repayment of capital and, therefore, they should require a lower rate of return. Additionally, interest paid on debt is a deductible expense for computation of tax liability whereas dividends are paid out of after-tax profit. Increased use of debt, therefore, is likely to lower the over-all cost of capital of the firm provided that the cost of equity remains unaffected. Financial risk is the chance that a firm would fail to meet its payment obligations. Capital structure of a company, thus, affects both the profitability and the financial risk. A capital structure will be said to be optimal when the proportion of debt and equity is such that it results in an increase in the value of the equity share. body: A company is estimating staffing needs for two units. For Unit X, planned task volume and the number of employees available have both increased. For Unit Y, planned task volume is unchanged while the number of employees available has decreased. The directions of change are known, but their magnitudes are not. Which approach should the managers use to determine whether each unit’s manpower requirement is met?
options: ["Assess each unit from workload alone, treating task volume as sufficient to determine staffing adequacy.","Assess each unit using both workload and workforce data before determining staffing adequacy.","Assess each unit from workforce alone, treating staff availability as sufficient to determine staffing adequacy.","Assess Unit X using both factors, but assess Unit Y from workload alone because its task volume is unchanged."]
explanation: The directions of change alone do not establish whether either unit has enough staff, since the stem gives no magnitudes. Estimating manpower requirements requires considering workload analysis and workforce analysis together. Therefore, B is the appropriate approach.

body:
A business is considering two available sources of finance. Source X has a lower cost but greater associated risk than Source Y; Source Y has a higher cost but lower associated risk. Which statement correctly describes how the business should compare the sources for optimal procurement?
(A) Compare the sources only by cost.
(B) Compare the sources only by associated risk.
(C) Note that both sources are available without comparing their costs or associated risks.
(D) Compare the sources by both cost and associated risk.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: ["Statement (A) only","Statement (B) only","Statement (C) only","Statement (D) only"]
explanation: For optimal procurement, available sources of finance are compared in terms of both their costs and associated risks. Statement (D) includes both dimensions of comparison.

Financial Management aims at reducing the cost of funds procured, keeping the risk under control and achieving effective deployment of such funds. It also aims at ensuring availability of enough funds whenever required as well as avoiding idle finance. body:
Match each activity or description with the staffing concept it primarily represents. Each concept is used once.

List-I
(A) Human resource personnel search for qualified people to work for the organisation.
(B) Managers throughout the organisation directly deal with and select people to work for it.
(C) Employees are helped to develop for efficient performance and career growth.
(D) The management function focuses on the human component of an organisation.

List-II
(I) Training and development
(II) Recruitment
(III) Staffing as a generic function of management
(IV) Staffing's focus on the human element

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation: Searching for qualified people is recruitment, and helping employees develop for efficient performance and career growth is training and development. The responsibility of managers throughout the organisation to deal with and select people shows that staffing is a generic management function; staffing focuses on the human component of the organisation.

body: A firm uses intermediaries to make its product available to buyers. Which intermediary activity is specifically identified as taking place after a sale?
options: ["Keeping the product in inventory","Demonstrating the product to potential buyers","Negotiating the product’s price with buyers","Servicing the product after the sale"]
explanation: Intermediary activities include keeping inventory, demonstrating the product, negotiating its price, closing sales and servicing the product after the sale. Servicing is the activity specifically identified as taking place after the sale.

The success of a market offer will depend on how well these ingredients are mixed to create superior value for the customers and simultaneously achieve their sale and profit objectives. For example, the purchase of a motorcycle provides functional utility of transportation, but at the same time satisfies the need for prestige and esteem and provides social benefit by the way of acceptance from a group, by riding a motorbike. topic: Financial Markets: focus on this supplied section: The Secondary Market is a place where an investor can buy/sell shares or securities from another investor rather than the issuer.. Test a distinct implication, application or calculation supported by it.
body: Arjun, an investor, owns shares that have already been issued. Nisha, also an investor, buys those shares directly from Arjun. Arjun receives the payment, and the issuer is not a party to this transaction. Which description is correct?
options: ["It is a primary-market transaction because Nisha acquires ownership of the shares.","It is a primary-market transaction because the issuer originally issued the shares.","It is not a market transaction because the issuer receives no payment.","It is a secondary-market transaction because one investor buys from another investor."]
explanation: A secondary-market transaction is one in which an investor buys or sells shares from another investor rather than the issuer. Here, Arjun and Nisha are both investors, and Arjun is the seller, so the transaction is in the secondary market. The issuer’s original role in issuing the shares does not change who is selling them in this transaction.

body: A company compares two selection routes. Route A selected 15 employees; 13 met its selection-stage benchmark and 9 met the stated on-the-job performance standard after six months. Route B selected 10 employees; 8 met its selection-stage benchmark and 7 met the same on-the-job standard after six months. The employees worked in comparable roles and conditions. For this comparison, effectiveness is measured by the proportion of selected employees who meet the on-the-job standard. Which route has the higher effectiveness on this measure?
options: ["Route A has the higher effectiveness.","Route B has the higher effectiveness.","The routes have equal effectiveness.","The stated information is insufficient to compare their effectiveness."]
explanation: The stated measure is the proportion of selected employees who meet the on-the-job standard. Route A’s proportion is 9/15, or 60%, while Route B’s is 7/10, or 70%; therefore, Route B has the higher effectiveness on this measure.

A company considering new borrowing prepares a cash-flow forecast that includes payments for normal business operations and investment in fixed assets. It excludes interest and principal repayments on the proposed borrowing and includes no buffer after fixed cash-payment obligations. Which statements correctly describe what the company should consider before borrowing?
(A) The forecast is sufficient to assess borrowing capacity because it includes operating and fixed-asset payments.
(B) The company should include the proposed interest and principal repayments among the cash-payment commitments considered.
(C) The projected cash flows should provide a buffer after covering the relevant fixed cash-payment obligations.
(D) The company may omit principal repayment because only interest is a debt-service cash commitment.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: ["(A) and (B) only","(A) and (D) only","(B) and (C) only","(C) and (D) only"]
explanation: Before borrowing, the company should consider whether projected cash flows cover fixed cash-payment obligations and leave a sufficient buffer. Those obligations include normal operations, fixed-asset investment, interest and principal repayment. Statement (A) is incorrect because the forecast omits debt service and a buffer; statement (D) is incorrect because principal repayment is also a debt-service commitment.

Match List-I with List-II. Each entry in List-II is to be used once.

List-I
(A) Physical product
(B) Benefit from the customer’s viewpoint
(C) Extended product
(D) Product decisions

List-II
(I) Decisions about features, quality, packaging, labelling and branding
(II) An item offered, such as televisions, refrigerators and colour monitors
(III) The result sought by buying toothpaste, such as whitening teeth or strengthening gums
(IV) After-sales services, handling complaints and availability of spare parts

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation: A physical product is the item offered, while a benefit from the customer’s viewpoint is the result for which the customer buys it. After-sales services, complaint handling and spare-parts availability are aspects of the extended product; features, quality, packaging, labelling and branding are product decisions. Option A swaps the customer benefit and extended product, option B swaps the physical product and product decisions, and option D mismatches all four descriptions.

Assume a community-run food bank is a social organisation. Arrange the following steps in the order of reasoning needed to apply the principle of management being all pervasive to this case, beginning with the case and ending with an inference.
(A) Infer that the food bank requires management.
(B) Identify the food bank as a social organisation.
(C) Apply the principle that management activities are common to economic, social and political organisations.
(D) Consider the community-run food bank as the case.
Choose the correct sequence from the options given below:
explanation: The sequence begins with the food bank, identifies it as a social organisation, applies the principle that management activities are common to social organisations, and then infers that it requires management. The other sequences place the classification or principle before the case, or apply the principle before identifying the organisation type.

body: A company replaces part of its equity financing with borrowed funds while keeping total capital unchanged. The cost of borrowed funds is lower than the cost of equity, and the cost of equity is assumed to remain unaffected by the change. No other financing terms change. What is the likely effect on the company’s overall cost of capital?
options: ["It is likely to decrease.","It is likely to increase.","It is likely to remain unchanged.","It cannot be predicted without knowing the exact proportion of debt."]
explanation: Replacing part of equity with debt increases the use of debt. The stated principle is that increased use of debt is likely to lower the overall cost of capital when the cost of equity remains unaffected; both conditions are satisfied here.

On the basis of ownership, the sources of business finance can be broadly classified into two categories viz., ‘owners’ funds’ and ‘borrowed funds’. Owners’ funds consist of equity share capital, preference share capital and reserves and surpluses or retained earnings. Borrowed funds can be in the form of loans, debentures, public deposits etc. These may be borrowed from banks, other financial institutions, debentureholders and public. Capital structure refers to the mix between owners and borrowed funds. These shall be referred as equity and debt in the subsequent text. It can be calculated as debt-equity ratio i.e., Debt Equity     or as the proportion of debt out of the total capital i.e., Debt Debt +E quity     . Debt and equity differ significantly in their cost and riskiness for the firm. The cost of debt is lower than the cost of equity for a firm because the lender’s risk is lower than the equity shareholder’s risk, since the lender earns an assured return and repayment of capital and, therefore, they should require a lower rate of return. Additionally, interest paid on debt is a deductible expense for computation of tax liability whereas dividends are paid out of after-tax profit. Increased use of debt, therefore, is likely to lower the over-all cost of capital of the firm provided that the cost of equity remains unaffected. Impact of a change in the debt-equity ratio upon the earning per share is dealt with in detail later in this chapter. Debt is cheaper but is more risky for a business because the payment of interest and the return of principal is obligatory for the business. Any default in meeting these commitments may force the business to go into liquidation. There is no such compulsion in case of equity, which is therefore, considered riskless for the business. Higher use of debt increases the fixed financial charges of a business. As a result, increased use of debt increases the financial risk of a company. Financial risk is the chance that a firm would fail to meet its payment obligations. Capital structure of a company, thus, affects both the profitability and the financial risk. A capital structure will be said to be optimal when the proportion of debt and equity is such that it results in an increase in the value of the equity share. In other words, all decisions relating to capital structure should emphasise on increasing the shareholders’ wealth. The proportion of debt in the overall capital is also called financial leverage. body:
An organisation is reviewing two employee-learning interventions. Intervention P is intended to increase employees’ knowledge and skills so that they can perform their present jobs better. Intervention Q is intended to support employees’ overall learning and growth and is career-oriented. Treat these descriptions as the intended purposes of the interventions.

Consider the following statements:
(A) P is development because increasing knowledge and skills is the defining feature of development.
(B) P is training because it is intended to help employees do their jobs better.
(C) Q is training because it is intended to help employees perform their present jobs better.
(D) Q is development because it is intended to support employees’ overall growth.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
(A) (A) and (C) only
(B) (B) and (D) only
(C) (A) and (D) only
(D) (B) and (C) only
options: ["(A) and (C) only","(B) and (D) only","(A) and (D) only","(B) and (C) only"]
explanation: P matches training because it increases knowledge and skills to enable better performance in the employee’s job. Q matches development because its intended purpose is overall employee growth and it is career-oriented. Therefore, statements (B) and (D) are correct.

topic: Organising: focus on this supplied section: Thus, a functional structure is an organisational design that groups similar or related jobs together. Advantages: The functional structure has many advantages to offer. Important . Test a distinct implication, application or calculation supported by it.
body:
A firm groups related jobs into departments according to function. Match each situation in List-I with the corresponding advantage in List-II.
List-I
(A) A new employee’s training is limited to a narrow range of skills used in the assigned function.
(B) A redesign reduces the repeated performance of the same activity by different teams.
(C) The organisational structure gives a place to each of the firm’s different functions.
(D) Employees in one department perform similar tasks.
List-II
(I) Training becomes easier because the focus is on a limited range of skills.
(II) Minimal duplication of effort supports economies of scale and lower cost.

body:
A company is preparing a long-term plan for launching a new service. The planning team identifies these actions:
(A) Set the long-term outcome the organisation intends to achieve.
(B) Set aside the staff, funds and equipment needed to achieve that outcome.
(C) Select the course of action for pursuing that outcome.
Arrange the actions in the order in which the dimensions of a comprehensive plan are presented.
explanation: The dimensions are presented in this order: determining long-term objectives, adopting a particular course of action, and allocating the resources necessary to achieve the objective. These correspond to (A), (C) and (B), respectively, so option D is correct.

body: A firm must choose a site for a warehouse used to store an agricultural product for a long period. Its stated objective in this decision is to minimise the transportation charges on the goods. Which location best fits this objective?
options: ["Near the production site, which helps minimise transportation charges for goods requiring long-term storage.","Near the market, which helps minimise transportation charges for goods requiring long-term storage.","At a larger number of market locations, which reduces the total cost of warehousing.","At a smaller number of market locations, which reduces the time required to serve customers."]
explanation: For an agricultural product requiring long-term storage, locating the warehouse near the production site helps minimise transportation charges. A market location does not fit this stated recommendation. The excerpt also establishes that more warehouses increase warehousing cost, while a larger number generally reduces the time taken to serve customers.

body:
Use this rule: a secondary-market transaction occurs when an investor buys securities from, or sells securities to, another investor rather than the issuer. In each case below, the named party is the direct counterparty.
(A) An investor buys shares from another investor.
(B) A company sells its shares directly to an investor.
(C) An investor sells securities directly to the issuing company.
(D) An investor sells securities to another investor.
Which transactions are secondary-market transactions?
options: ["(A) and (B) only","(A) and (C) only","(A) and (D) only","(B) and (D) only"]
explanation: Transactions (A) and (D) are between investors, so they fit the stated rule. In (B) and (C), the company issuing the securities is the direct counterparty, so those transactions do not fit the rule.

body:
Match List-I with List-II. Each case reports a specific result. Match it with the training-and-development purpose or outcome it directly illustrates.

List-I
(A) After a training intervention, the number of units produced per shift rises, while product quality is unchanged.
(B) After a training intervention, product quality improves, while the number of units produced per shift is unchanged.
(C) A development programme increases employees’ ability to perform duties they will take up in a later period; no current productivity or profit change is reported.
(D) Employee productivity improves, and higher profits follow; the case does not report a separate change in quantity or quality.

List-II
(I) Increasing an employee’s ability to perform to improve future performance.
(II) Enhancing employee productivity in terms of quantity.
(III) Enhancing employee productivity in terms of quality.
(IV) Higher profits resulting from enhanced productivity.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
A. (A)-(I), (B)-(II), (C)-(III), (D)-(IV)
B. (A)-(II), (B)-(I), (C)-(IV), (D)-(III)
C. (A)-(III), (B)-(IV), (C)-(I), (D)-(II)
D. (A)-(II), (B)-(III), (C)-(I), (D)-(IV)
explanation: The increase in units produced in A illustrates productivity in terms of quantity, while the quality improvement in B illustrates productivity in terms of quality. C describes increased ability to perform future duties, and D identifies higher profits following improved productivity.

A firm has taken a capital-budgeting decision that is expected to increase the scale of its operations. It is preparing a financial plan to ensure that funds are available whenever required. Arrange the following considerations in a logical sequence, from estimating fund requirements to matching requirements with availability.
(A) Specify possible sources of funds
(B) Estimate funds required for different purposes
(C) Match fund requirements with their availability
(D) Estimate when the funds are to be made available
Choose the correct sequence from the options given below:
explanation: Financial planning aims to ensure that funds are available whenever required. The plan estimates funds needed for different purposes and when they are needed, specifies possible sources, and seeks a proper match between fund requirements and availability; hence the sequence is B-D-A-C.

Financial Planning Financial planning is essentially the preparation of a financial blueprint of an organisation’s future operations. The objective of financial planning is to ensure that enough funds are available at right time. If adequate funds are not available the firm will not be able to honour its commitments and carry out its plans. On the other hand, if excess funds are available, it will unnecessarily add to the cost and may encourage wasteful expenditure. It must be kept in mind that financial planning is not equivalent to, or a substitute for, financial management. Financial management aims at choosing the best investment and financing alternatives by focusing on their costs and benefits. Its objective is to increase the shareholders’ wealth. Financial planning on the other hand aims at smooth operations by focusing on fund requirements and their availability in the light of financial decisions. For example, if a capital budgeting decisions is taken, the operations are likely to be at a higher scale. The amount of expenses and revenues are likely to increase. Financial planning process tries to forecast all the items which are likely to undergo changes. It enables the management to foresee the fund requirements both the quantum as well as the timing. Likely shortage and surpluses are forecast so that necessary activities are taken in advance to meet those situations. Thus, financial planning strives to achieve the following twin objectives. (a) To ensure availability of funds whenever requir ed: This include a proper estimation of the funds required for different purposes such as for the purchase of long- term assets or to meet day-to- day expenses of business etc. Apart from this, there is a need to estimate the time at which these funds are to be made available. Financial planning also tries to specify possible sources of these funds. (b) To see tha t the firm does not raise resources unnecessarily: Excess funding is almost as bad as inadequate funding. Even if there is some surplus money, good financial planning would put it to the best possible use so that the financial resources are not left idle and don’t unnecessarily add to the cost. Thus, a proper matching of funds requirements and their availability is sought to be achieved by financial planning. body: Initially, an identical product costs ₹12,000 in India and US$200 in the United States, and the exchange rate is ₹60 per US dollar. The Indian price then rises by 25% and the US price rises by 20%. Assuming zero transportation costs and a long-run exchange-rate adjustment that makes the product cost the same in both countries, what is the implied exchange rate?
options: ["₹60 per US dollar","₹62.50 per US dollar","₹75 per US dollar","₹57.60 per US dollar"]
explanation: After the price rises, the product costs ₹15,000 in India and US$240 in the United States. Equal prices after conversion require ₹15,000 ÷ US$240 = ₹62.50 per US dollar. This exchange rate makes US$240 equivalent to ₹15,000.

I. The policy is import substitution.
II. It aims to replace imports with domestic production.
III. It aims to replace domestic production with imports.
IV. It uses tariffs alone, not quotas, as forms of protection.

explanation: The described policy matches import substitution because it replaces imports with domestic production. Statements I and II are therefore correct; III reverses that direction, and IV is inconsistent with the stated use of both tariffs and quotas.

body: A district divides residents into Group P, which is already well served, and Group Q, which has limited access to services. The district plans additional public outlays for education and health, with the aim of pursuing economic growth and equity together. Each plan describes where the additional outlays extend services; “only” means that the proposed extension does not reach the other group. Which plan best applies this objective?
options: ["Extend education to both Groups P and Q, but extend health only to Group P.","Extend education only to Group P, but extend health to both Groups P and Q.","Extend education to both Groups P and Q, and extend health to both Groups P and Q.","Extend education only to Group P and health only to Group Q."]
explanation: The stated principle is to spread both education and health services across different sections of society so that economic growth and equity are pursued together. Plan C extends each service to both groups. Plans A and B leave one service confined to one group, while Plan D does not spread either service across both groups.

body: A rural producer group has 18 members. Each member delivers 24 crates of produce that meet the agreed quality standard, and all 432 crates are accepted for procurement. Under an assured-procurement arrangement, every accepted crate is purchased at the pre-decided price of ₹1,250, with no deductions or other payments. A spot-market quote of ₹1,500 per crate is available, but none of the produce is sold at that quote. What is the total amount payable to the group under the arrangement?
explanation: The group delivers 18 × 24 = 432 crates, and the stem states that all are accepted for procurement. At ₹1,250 per crate, the total payment is 432 × ₹1,250 = ₹5,40,000. The spot-market quote does not apply because none of the produce is sold at that price.

In each case, the initially announced fixed exchange rate is ₹80 per unit of foreign currency. The quote is expressed in rupees per unit of foreign currency, and the change is made by the government. Calculate the percentage change relative to ₹80 and match each case with its interpretation.

List-I
(A) The government raises the quote from ₹80 to ₹88.
(B) The government lowers the quote from ₹80 to ₹72.
(C) The government raises the quote from ₹80 to ₹84.
(D) The government lowers the quote from ₹80 to ₹76.

List-II
(I) Increase of 10%; devaluation; domestic currency becomes cheaper
(II) Decrease of 10%; revaluation; domestic currency becomes costlier
(III) Increase of 5%; devaluation; domestic currency becomes cheaper
(IV) Decrease of 5%; revaluation; domestic currency becomes costlier

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation: The changes from ₹80 are ₹8 for (A) and (B), or 10%, and ₹4 for (C) and (D), or 5%. An increase in the exchange rate in a fixed system is devaluation, which makes the domestic currency cheaper; a decrease is revaluation, which makes it costlier. Therefore, the matching in option A is correct.

In other words, the currency will maintain a stable purchasing power. Without this confidence, a currency will not be used as an international medium of exchange and unit of account since there is no international authority with the power to force the use of a particular currency in international transactions. In the past, governments have tried to gain confidence of potential users by announcing that the national currency will be freely convertible at a fixed price into another asset. Also, the issuing authority will have no control over the value of that asset into which the currency can be converted. This other asset most often has been gold, or other national currencies. There are two aspects of this commitment that has affected its credibility — the ability to convert freely in unlimited amounts and the price at which this conversion takes place. The international monetary system has been set up to handle these issues and ensure stability in international transactions. With the increase in the volume of transactions, gold ceased to be the asset into which national currencies could be converted (See Box 6.2). Although some national currencies have international acceptability, what is important in transactions between two countries is the currency in which the trade occurs. For instance, if an Indian wants to buy a good made in America, she would need dollars to complete the transaction. If the price of the good is ten dollars, she would need to know how much it would cost her in Indian rupees. That is, she will need to know the price of dollar in terms of rupees. The price of one currency in terms of another currency is known as the foreign exchange rate or simply the exchange rate . We will discuss this in detail in section 6.2. 6.1 THE BALANCE OF PAYMENTS The balance of payments (BoP) record the transactions in goods, services and assets between residents of a country with the rest of the world for a specified time period typically a year. There are two main accounts in the BoP — the current account and the capital account1. 6.1.1 Current Account Current Account is the record of trade in goods and services and transfer payments. Figure 6.1 illustrates the components of Current Account. Trade in goods includes exports and imports of goods. Trade in services includes factor income and non-factor income transactions. Transfer payments are the receipts which the residents of a country get for ‘free’, without having to provide any goods or services in return. They consist of gifts, remittances and grants. They could be given by the government or by private citizens living abroad. 1 There is a new classification in which the balance of payments have been divided into three accounts — the current account, the financial account and the capital account. This is as per the new accounting standards specified by the International Monetary Fund (IMF) in the sixth edition of the Balance of Payments and International Investment Position Manual (BPM6). India has also made the change but the Reserve Bank of India continues to publish data accounting to the old classification. body: An employment survey records each worker once under one principal industry. It reports 24 workers in agriculture, 12 in mining and quarrying, 18 in construction, 16 in trade and 10 in services. For this case, agriculture and mining/quarrying are primary activities, construction is secondary, and trade and services are tertiary/service activities; secondary and tertiary/service sectors are treated as non-farm sectors. What percentage of all surveyed workers is employed in non-farm sectors?
explanation: The non-farm workers are those in construction, trade and services: 18 + 16 + 10 = 44. The total surveyed workforce is 24 + 12 + 18 + 16 + 10 = 80, so the non-farm share is (44/80) × 100 = 55%.
